title: Luke Slaughter of Tombstone
paragraphs: A late-era adult Western starring Sam Buffington as Luke Slaughter, a tough cattleman and former cavalry officer facing danger in Arizona Territory near Tombstone.
Late-era CBS adult Western starring Sam Buffington as former cavalryman turned Arizona cattleman Luke Slaughter, with Junius Matthews as Wichita.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: CBS run (February 23, 1958 to June 15, 1958) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Junius Matthews (performer), Sam Buffington (performer), William N. Robson (director, producer, and radio adaptor), Tom Hanley (editorial supervisor and sound patterns), Wilbur Hatch (composer, conductor, and music), Amerigo Moreno (conductor, composer, and music supervisor), and Fran Van Hartesfeldt (writer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]], and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]].

The stories often return to late network-radio drama, cattle ranching and cattle drives, Tombstone and Arizona Territory, adult radio Western, frontier law, violence and justice, and frontier business and cattle economy.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Post-Civil War Arizona Territory cattle frontier, Late-era CBS network radio Western, One-off OBrien Paints sponsorship, and April 6, 1958 pre-emption.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|suspense|Suspense]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|cbs-radio-workshop|CBS Radio Workshop]], [[show|escape|Escape]], and [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]].
